title: Stop bleeding
lead: Call 911 first if you have any signal.
source: Stop the Bleed guidance and ATP 3-50.21

steps.title: Press hard
steps.body: Put cloth or gauze on the wound and push down firmly with both hands. Do not lift to check.

steps.title: Arm or leg still bleeding?
steps.body: Apply a tourniquet 2–3 inches above the wound, not on a joint. Tighten until bleeding stops.

steps.title: Note the time
steps.body: Write the time the tourniquet went on. Do not loosen it.

steps.title: Wound on body or neck?
steps.body: Pack it tightly with gauze or clean cloth, then keep pressing until help arrives.

title: CPR for an adult
lead: Hands-only CPR, for a teen or adult who suddenly collapses. Call 911 on speaker.
source: American Heart Association hands-only CPR and American Red Cross first aid guidance

steps.title: Check and call
steps.body: Tap the shoulder and shout. If there is no response and no normal breathing, call 911 and put the phone on speaker.

steps.title: Hands on the chest
steps.body: Place the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, your other hand on top, fingers laced. Keep your arms straight.

steps.title: Push hard and fast
steps.body: Push straight down at least 2 inches, 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come all the way back up between pushes.

steps.title: Do not stop
steps.body: Keep going until the person moves and breathes, or until someone takes over. Swap with another person every two minutes if you can.

steps.title: Use an AED when it arrives
steps.body: Turn it on and follow the spoken instructions. Restart compressions as soon as it tells you to.

title: Make water safe
lead: Boiling is the surest way. Use bleach only when you cannot boil.
source: CDC: Making Water Safe in an Emergency; EPA emergency disinfection of drinking water

steps.title: Clear it first
steps.body: Let cloudy water settle, then pour it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter.

steps.title: Boil if you can
steps.body: Bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes. Let it cool on its own.

steps.title: No heat? Use plain bleach
steps.body: Per gallon of clear water, add 8 drops of unscented 6% household bleach, or 6 drops of 8.25%. Stir well.

steps.title: Wait 30 minutes
steps.body: The water should smell faintly of bleach. If it does not, repeat the dose and wait another 15 minutes.

steps.title: Store it covered
steps.body: Keep treated water in clean, covered containers out of sunlight.

title: Hypothermia
lead: Call 911. Shivering that stops on its own is a bad sign, not a good one.
source: CDC guidance on hypothermia and cold stress

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: Adults: shivering, slurred speech, clumsy hands, confusion, drowsiness. Babies: bright red, cold skin and very low energy.

steps.title: Get out of the cold
steps.body: Move the person into a warm room or shelter. Handle them gently and keep them lying still.

steps.title: Take off wet clothes
steps.body: Remove anything wet and dry the skin.

steps.title: Warm the middle first
steps.body: Cover the chest, neck, head and groin with blankets, or use skin-to-skin contact under a blanket. Do not rub the arms and legs.

steps.title: Warm drinks only if fully awake
steps.body: Give warm, sweet, non-alcoholic drinks. Never give alcohol, and never give anything to someone who cannot swallow.

steps.title: Keep them covered
steps.body: Once they start to warm, wrap the whole body including the head and keep them still until help arrives.

title: Signal for help
lead: Text instead of calling — short messages get through when calls do not.
source: FEMA / Ready.gov guidance on communicating during a disaster

steps.title: Text, do not call
steps.body: Send a short text. Voice calls tie up the networks that emergency crews need.

steps.title: Save your battery
steps.body: Turn on low-power mode, dim the screen and close everything you are not using.

steps.title: Tell your out-of-area contact
steps.body: Message the contact in your plan and let them pass the word on to everyone else.

steps.title: Make yourself seen and heard
steps.body: Three of anything means distress: three whistle blasts, three flashes, three fires. Use a mirror or bright cloth by day.

steps.title: Stay where you are if you can
steps.body: Rescuers search last known locations. If you must move, leave a note saying where you are going and when you left.

title: Shelter in place
lead: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned.
source: FEMA / Ready.gov shelter-in-place guidance; CDC carbon monoxide guidance

steps.title: Get everyone inside
steps.body: Bring people and pets in. Lock the doors and close the windows, vents and fireplace damper.

steps.title: Pick an interior room
steps.body: Choose a small room with as few windows as possible, and take your kit and radio with you.

steps.title: Turn off air movement
steps.body: Shut off fans, heating and air conditioning so outside air is not pulled in.

steps.title: Seal the room only if told to
steps.body: If officials report a chemical or radiological release, tape plastic sheeting over the doors, windows and vents of that room.

steps.title: Listen for the all-clear
steps.body: Keep a battery or hand-crank radio on NOAA Weather Radio and wait for officials to say it is safe.

steps.title: Never burn fuel indoors
steps.body: No generator, grill or camp stove inside, in a garage or near a window. Carbon monoxide has no smell and kills.

title: Choking
lead: Can't cough, speak or breathe? Act now. Have someone call 911.
source: American Red Cross choking first aid (adult); American Heart Association

steps.title: Ask: are you choking?
steps.body: If they can cough hard or speak, let them keep coughing. Stay with them.

steps.title: Give 5 back blows
steps.body: Stand behind them and lean them forward. Hit firmly between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand, 5 times.

steps.title: Give 5 belly thrusts
steps.body: Make a fist just above the belly button. Grab it with your other hand. Pull in and up, hard and fast, 5 times.

steps.title: Keep going
steps.body: Switch between 5 back blows and 5 belly thrusts until the object comes out or they can breathe, cough or speak.

steps.title: Pregnant or very large?
steps.body: Put your fist on the center of the chest instead of the belly, and pull straight back.

steps.title: If they pass out
steps.body: Lower them to the floor, call 911 and start CPR. Look in the mouth and take out any object you can see.

title: Burns
lead: Cool the burn with running water. No ice, butter or grease.
source: American Red Cross burn first aid; CDC burn safety

steps.title: Stop the burning
steps.body: Get away from the heat. If clothing is on fire: stop, drop and roll.

steps.title: Cool it
steps.body: Hold the burn under cool running water for at least 10 minutes. Do not use ice, butter or ointment.

steps.title: Take off rings and tight things
steps.body: Remove jewelry and tight clothing near the burn before it swells. Leave anything stuck to the skin.

steps.title: Cover it loosely
steps.body: Use a clean, dry, non-stick cloth or sterile gauze. Do not break blisters.

steps.title: Call 911 for a bad burn
steps.body: Large burns; burns on the face, hands, feet or groin; deep burns that look white, brown or charred; chemical or electrical burns; or trouble breathing after a fire.

title: Heat stroke
lead: Heat stroke can kill. Call 911 and cool them fast.

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: Very hot body, confusion, slurred speech, fainting or seizures. The skin may be hot and dry, or soaked with sweat.

steps.title: Call 911
steps.body: Heat stroke is an emergency. Do not wait to see if it gets better.

steps.title: Move them to shade
steps.body: Get them out of the sun into a cool place. Take off extra clothing.

steps.title: Cool them fast
steps.body: Put them in cold water if you can. If not, soak their skin and clothes with water, fan them, and put ice or cold wet cloths on the neck, armpits and groin.

steps.title: No drinks if confused
steps.body: Give nothing to drink if they are confused or not fully awake.

steps.title: Only weak, dizzy and sweaty?
steps.body: That may be heat exhaustion. Move them somewhere cool, loosen clothing, use cool wet cloths and give sips of water. Get help if they throw up, get worse, or are not better in an hour.

title: Severe allergic reaction
lead: Trouble breathing or swelling after a sting, food or medicine? Use epinephrine and call 911.
source: American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology; American Red Cross anaphylaxis guidance

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: Trouble breathing, wheezing, swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, hives, throwing up, or feeling faint.

steps.title: Use their epinephrine
steps.body: If they have an auto-injector (such as an EpiPen), help them use it right away. Press it into the outer thigh, through clothing if needed, as the label shows.

steps.title: Call 911
steps.body: Call even if they feel better. The reaction can come back.

steps.title: Lay them down
steps.body: If they feel faint, lay them flat and raise their legs. If breathing is hard, let them sit up. Do not let them stand or walk.

steps.title: Not better?
steps.body: If there is no improvement after 5 to 15 minutes and they have a second auto-injector, use it.

steps.title: If they stop breathing
steps.body: Start CPR.

title: Stroke
lead: Note the time the signs started and call 911. Every minute counts.
source: American Stroke Association (BE FAST); CDC stroke signs and symptoms

steps.title: Face
steps.body: Ask them to smile. Does one side of the face droop?

steps.title: Arms
steps.body: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift down?

steps.title: Speech
steps.body: Ask them to repeat a short sentence. Is the speech slurred or strange?

steps.title: Balance and eyes
steps.body: Sudden loss of balance, or sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes, are signs too.

steps.title: Time: call 911
steps.body: Any one of these signs: call 911 now. Write down the time the signs started. Doctors need it.

steps.title: While you wait
steps.body: Keep them still and comfortable. Give nothing to eat or drink. Do not let them drive or sleep it off.

title: Broken bone
lead: Keep it still. Do not try to straighten it.
source: American Red Cross first aid; Mayo Clinic first aid: fractures

steps.title: Neck or back hurt?
steps.body: Do not move them at all unless they are in danger where they are. Call 911.

steps.title: Call 911 if
steps.body: Bone shows through the skin, there is heavy bleeding, they do not respond, or the hip, thigh or pelvis may be broken.

steps.title: Stop any bleeding
steps.body: Press on the wound with a clean cloth. See the Stop bleeding card.

steps.title: Keep it still
steps.body: Support it the way you found it. Do not push a bone back in or straighten the limb.

steps.title: Splint it
steps.body: Pad a stiff object, such as a board or rolled newspaper, and tie it along the injury so the joints above and below cannot move. If fingers or toes turn pale, cold or numb, loosen it.

steps.title: Cold and calm
steps.body: Put a wrapped cold pack on it. If they turn pale, faint or breathe fast, lay them down, keep them warm, and raise the legs if the legs, hips and back are not hurt.

title: Seizure
lead: Keep them safe. Do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth.
source: CDC: Seizure first aid; Epilepsy Foundation

steps.title: Time it
steps.body: Look at a clock when the seizure starts.

steps.title: Make space
steps.body: Ease them to the floor. Move hard or sharp things away. Put something soft under the head. Loosen anything around the neck.

steps.title: Turn them on their side
steps.body: This helps them breathe. Do not hold them down. Put nothing in their mouth.

steps.title: Call 911 if
steps.body: It lasts more than 5 minutes, another seizure follows, they have trouble breathing or do not wake up, they are hurt, it happened in water, or it is their first seizure.

steps.title: Stay with them
steps.body: Stay until they are fully awake. Talk calmly. They may be confused for a while.

title: Poison
lead: Call Poison Help: 1-800-222-1222. Free, any time, day or night.
source: America's Poison Centers; HRSA Poison Help line

steps.title: Not awake or not breathing?
steps.body: Call 911 right away. Start CPR if they are not breathing.

steps.title: Call Poison Help
steps.body: Call 1-800-222-1222. Have the container with you. Experts tell you what to do.

steps.title: Do not make them throw up
steps.body: Only do it if Poison Help tells you to.

steps.title: On the skin
steps.body: Take off any clothing it touched. Rinse the skin with running water for 15 to 20 minutes.

steps.title: In the eye
steps.body: Rinse the eye with lukewarm running water for 15 to 20 minutes.

steps.title: Fumes
steps.body: Get to fresh air right away. Carbon monoxide has no smell: leave the building if a CO alarm sounds or several people feel sick, dizzy or sleepy.

title: Flood
lead: Turn around, don't drown. Six inches of moving water can knock you down.
source: National Weather Service: Turn Around Don't Drown; Ready.gov floods

steps.title: Get to high ground
steps.body: If you are told to leave, leave. If water is rising, move to higher ground now.

steps.title: Do not walk in moving water
steps.body: Six inches of fast water can knock you down.

steps.title: Do not drive into water
steps.body: One foot of moving water can float a car. Two feet can sweep away an SUV or truck. Turn around.

steps.title: Car in fast water?
steps.body: Stay inside. If water rises inside the car, get out onto the roof.

steps.title: Trapped in a building?
steps.body: Go to the highest floor. Do not climb into a closed attic. Go on the roof only if you must, then signal for help.

steps.title: After the water
steps.body: Stay out of floodwater. It can hide sharp objects, sewage and live power lines.

title: Lost outdoors
lead: Stop. Stay put. Being found is easier than finding your way.
source: National Park Service and U.S. Forest Service: STOP (Stop, Think, Observe, Plan)

steps.title: Stop
steps.body: As soon as you think you are lost, stop moving. Sit down, drink some water and calm down.

steps.title: Think
steps.body: How did you get here? What do you remember passing? Do not walk on unless you are sure.

steps.title: Observe
steps.body: Check the Map tab (it works with no signal), the sun and the land around you.

steps.title: Plan: stay put
steps.body: If you are not sure of the way, stay where you are. Searchers start where you were last seen.

steps.title: Be seen and heard
steps.body: Three of anything means help: three whistle blasts, three shouts, three flashes of a light. Spread bright colors in the open.

steps.title: Stay warm and dry
steps.body: Get out of wind and rain, and off the cold ground. Text someone your location if you get any signal.
